Results.ReviewText:
I’m actually sorry that I bought this unit. It had so many good reviews, and I don’t need a large grill, but my old rounded top Grill worked better.
I find the greats are too far apart. It uses much more gas than my old unit. And it just doesn’t cook as well. The one page of instructions in the booklet are for one hard to read because they’re in tiny print, but they don’t really get into the subtlety or not so subtle aspects of grilling things on this grill. Even when I use the enhanced boost function on two of the grills, I don’t get a nice Seer the way I did on my old model. I think Weber, it would be great if you actually created a handout and/or some YouTube videos showing people actually cooking different food on this grill from beginning to end. There’s plenty of stuff about how to light it and basically heat it up.
In terms of its size and maneuverability it’s just fine. The new coating on the fold up ledges is great except it’s very slippery. So if you put a plate or Pyrex on it, you have to put as I do some kind of gripper underneath or it’ll slide right off.
And I would love to understand why it uses up so much propane. The old Grill would last seemingly forever. I’ve only cooked maybe 6 to 8 small items on this grill and it used 3/4 of the tank.
Anyway, I am not a fan of this model. And I’m sorry I bought it.
Results.Title: Unhappy with this one

Results.ReviewText: I love the grill! It cooks great and don’t have any issues as of yet with it. I got this to replace the SPIRIT E-210 I had for 10 years. What I love about this one versus my old one is that the grease tray slides out from the back to clean versus my old one which slid out through the front which was kind of a pain to remove. The only thing I’m not real happy about is my old grill had 4 casters and the grill was able to move with ease. The new one has 2 regular wheels to the right side and nothing on the left side which makes it very hard to maneuver if you need to move the grill out from where you are storing it on your patio. Hopefully they could come out with some adapter wheels that you could attach somehow to make this problem go away. 🙏
Results.Title: Love my New Grill so far but……

Results.ReviewText: Grill will not ignite. I called customer service and they indicated that it was the regulator and that a new one would be sent to me.  I have yet to receive the part and it has been 4 weeks.  I found a regulator and hose at a local store and purchased it.  The problem persists and the grill will not ignite.  I have had two Weber grills and trusted the brand and quality, but now I am concerned.  I returned to Lowes last evening and they are coming to pick it up.  I will then request that I receive another E-325 that has been tested before it is delivered to me.  If that one does not work, I will again return it and never buy another Weber grill.

Results.ReviewText:
This 325 is not well built as may 12 year old spirit 3xx. Only two wheels not 4. The legs with no wheels rests on the concrete. They will rust quickly if you don’t put some kind of skids on them. 
The width is 2” less than the original. 
The cover handle looks nice but gets vert hot in the sun. You have to use mittens in the hot supper sun. The original did not have this problem it was a cool to the touch material. 
The back is expanded metal, This makes it less sturdy. 
The sear feature just brings the heat output to the high setting on the original. 
In short, Weber has cheapened the Spirit product. On the plus side, heat is very even across the surface. The flavor bards are SS.
The grates are a better design.

Results.ReviewText:
There are two or three things that are disappointing to me. 1st you recommend to bring it up to 500° to start. It's very difficult to control the temperature after that and lower it. It stays at 500 which is too hot sometimes for what I'm doing. My older spirit which worked for 18 years was much better with the controls of the heat. 
Secondly my all the spirit had a hook to hang the propane tank so you knew when it was nearing empty and you wouldn't run out in the middle of cooking. This new one just sits inside under the grill, and there's no way of knowing how much propane is left.
Results.Title: Not happy with my new spirit E325

Results.ReviewText: I like this grill. Both shelves do fold down which was hard to determine from online retailer listings. It gets nice and hot quickly when I need it to. The cast iron grates are heavier than other grills that I considered. Always a good cook. For the price point though, the grill should have casters on the two fixed legs. People likely choose this model because it is space saving and those casters would greatly help to tuck this into a tight deck space when not in use. Read the 10 year warranty closely, only some parts are guaranteed 10 years. The grates 5 years. The grease tray assembly, looks to only have two years. This part seems vulnerable to rust from moisture that is attracted to salts accumulated from food drippings but it is easy to remove and clean occasionally so hopefully there will not be a rust problem. Overall a great grill except for my two pet peeves of casters and warranty fine print.
